Subject: Re: Fwd: Production — 5xx/429 spike (since 07:50 PST)

Preliminary triage from infra:
- Correlation confirms a mix of 429s and 5xx from a subset of inference nodes serving rwi-1.3-q6.
- Root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel selection path is falling back to a slower execution path for requests with variable sequence lengths >1024. That path increases latency and causes in-flight request queues to grow. When in-flight queues hit the worker's limits, the runtime responds 429 to upstream, which in turn triggers client retries and a retry storm.
- Observed KV cache growth on the affected nodes (heap growth + GC pressure) likely due to a corner-case in the q6 kernel's KV eviction when sequence length spikes.

Data points attached:
- flame: inference-flamegraph-0800.svg (hot path shows fallback kernel and GC spikes)
- autoscaler snapshot: autoscaler-metrics-0800.csv (no scale event during the initial surge — metric used was cpu, not pending requests)

Immediate mitigations to propose (choose one):
A) Rollback model variant for Nimbus to rwi-1.3 (non-quant) — fast, high confidence.
B) Toggle quantization_profile for Nimbus to q4hf (less aggressive) — potential immediate improvement but untested for corner-case.
C) Apply runtime hotfix: limit per-worker concurrency and enforce backoff headers to avoid retry amplification — more work, but reduces blast radius.

I recommend A for immediate customer impact reduction and then B/C as follow-ups while we root-cause. I'll open INF-3492 and attach logs.

Attachments: inference-flamegraph-0800.svg, autoscaler-metrics-0800.csv

Update — rollback completed at 09:22 PST. Post-rollback observations: overall 5xx rate dropped ~92% in the affected cluster within 10 minutes. 429s reduced substantially, end-to-end latency back near baseline. We are still seeing a residual retry storm (clients spamming retries) which is causing sporadic spikes in pending requests; we pushed a short-term mitigation:
- Enabled short-term rate limiting at the front door for Nimbus (100 requests/s per region) and a 2s enforced backoff header for 429 responses.
- Opened INF-3492 (https://jira.redwood.local/browse/INF-3492) to track a fix in the quantized kernel and KV eviction logic.

Team — closing loop for today. Quick executive summary for records and the customer:
- Timeline: Quantized variant rwi-1.3-q6 rolled at ~06:30 PST. Customer errors started ~07:50 PST. Rollback to rwi-1.3 completed by 09:22 PST.
- Impact: transient increase in 5xx/429s and elevated latency for Nimbus Health in us-west-2. Customer-facing errors peaked for ~45 minutes before rollback; residual retry amplification took longer to quiet.
- Root cause (initial): fallback in quantized kernel selection + KV cache eviction anomaly on corner-case seq lengths caused extra latency and worker saturation.
- Mitigation: rollback, short-term front-door rate limits and backoff headers, created INF-3492.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Soojin: kernel/kv regression root-cause and patch (ETA 72h).
- Hannah: autoscaler policy update to include pending requests and 429-based scaling (ETA 7d).
- Marissa: customer exec brief and SLA credit proposal (ETA 48h).
- Marcus: coordinate postmortem and synced SLAs with Sales/GTM (ETA 48h).

We should also add a test to the release harness to validate KV eviction behavior for sequence length distributions that mimic customer traffic. I'll flag this for the release checklist immediately.
